mainTopic: Who may carry the blood (הולכה), and questions about scooping the קטורת: by another כהן, after the כהן גדול dies, and whether he scoops a second time inside.
overview: The גמרא opens with a ברייתא saying that if a זר or another unfit person does הולכה, carrying the blood, the service is פסול. This refutes רב ששת. The גמרא explains that רב ששת ruled before he knew this ברייתא, and later used it against רב חסדא. It also explains that רב חסדא's פסוק only shows the לויים stood holding the blood like benches. Next, רב פפא asks whether a handful of קטורת scooped by another כהן is valid, and the question ends in תיקו. רבי יהושע בן לוי then asks whether a replacement כהן גדול may enter with the handful scooped by a כהן גדול who died. This leads to a side discussion about רבי חנינא's praise of the question, whether רבי חנינא was older, and his medical expertise. רב פפא and רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע disagree about how the answer depends on whether the כהן גדול scoops a second time inside. The גמרא tries to settle that question from the משנה, rejects the proof, and begins a new proof that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: A ברייתא disqualifies carrying the blood by unfit people
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב ששת's earlier ruling with a ברייתא. It lists four kinds of unfit people and three blood services, and adds that sitting or using the left hand also makes the service פסול.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged: If a non-כהן, a mourner on his first day, a drunk כהן, or a כהן with a blemish does receiving, carrying, or sprinkling of the blood, it is invalid. Likewise if he sits, or uses his left hand, it is invalid.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא to attack רב ששת's ruling from just before this section. That ruling was lenient about הולכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The key word is הולכה. The ברייתא puts carrying in the same list as קבלה and זריקה, so carrying counts as a real עבודה. That means it must be done by a fit כהן, standing, with his right hand, which goes against רב ששת's lenient view.

keyTerms.meaning: A mourner on the first day, before the burial
Receiving the blood in a vessel
Carrying the blood to the מזבח
Sprinkling the blood on the מזבח

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
A non-priest, a mourner, a drunk one, and a blemished one,
phrases.notes: Four kinds of people unfit to do the עבודה

phrases.english: in receiving, carrying, or sprinkling, it is invalid.
phrases.notes: Carrying is listed as a full עבודה

phrases.english: And likewise sitting, and likewise the left hand, it is invalid!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב ששת's ruling, which was stated on the previous amud.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב ששת's lenient ruling regarding הולכה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא treats הולכה as a full עבודה that a זר or other unfit person invalidates, which contradicts the lenient view.

steps.title: Conclusive refutation
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא accepts the challenge as final, and רב ששת's ruling is rejected.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is a refutation.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא says the ברייתא fully refutes רב ששת. There is no answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An אמורא cannot argue with a ברייתא, so his view falls. The next step will ask how רב ששת could have said this at all.

keyTerms.meaning: A conclusive refutation that has no answer

phrases.english: It is a conclusive refutation.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts the challenge from step 1 as decisive.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Carrying the blood by a זר, or by any other unfit person, is פסול. רב ששת's lenient ruling is rejected.

steps.title: But רב ששת himself challenged רב חסדא on this
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how רב ששת could be refuted by this ברייתא when he himself used it. It tells the story: רב ששת asked רב חסדא whether הולכה by a זר is valid, and רב חסדא said it is כשר, quoting a פסוק from דברי הימים.
steps.simpleTranslation: But wasn't it רב ששת who used this ברייתא as a challenge? רב ששת told רב חסדא's spokesman to ask him: What is the law of carrying by a non-כהן? He answered: It is valid, and a פסוק supports me: 'They slaughtered the פסח, and the כהנים sprinkled from their hand, and the לויים skinned.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is surprised that רב ששת would rule against a ברייתא he clearly knew. It is setting up the proof of this by telling the story with רב חסדא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב חסדא read the words 'מידם' to mean that the כהנים took the blood from the hands of the לויים. That would show the לויים, who are not כהנים, carried the blood, so הולכה by a זר would be כשר. This story sets up step 4, where רב ששת attacks that view using our ברייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: But isn't it so that (opens a surprised challenge)
The spokesman who announced the teacher's words aloud to the audience

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two people. רב חסדא is the one who said הולכה by a זר is כשר. רב ששת is the one who asked him the question and then challenged him.

phrases.english: But wasn't it Rav Sheshet who raised it as an objection?

phrases.aramaic: דַּאֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב שֵׁשֶׁת לְאָמוֹרֵיהּ דְּרַב חִסְדָּא,
phrases.english: For Rav Sheshet said to Rav Ḥisda's interpreter,
Ask this of Rav Ḥisda:
What is the law of carrying done by a non-priest?
He said to him: It is valid,
and a verse supports me:
"And they slaughtered the Paschal offering
and the priests sprinkled from their hand,
phrases.notes: רב חסדא reads 'their hand' as the hand of the לויים

phrases.english: and the Levites flayed"! (דברי הימים ב לה:יא)

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions how the refutation in step 2 makes sense, given what רב ששת himself said elsewhere.
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that רב ששת ruled against this ברייתא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רב ששת himself quoted this ברייתא against רב חסדא, so he knew it. How, then, could he rule against it?

steps.title: רב ששת quotes the same ברייתא against רב חסדא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows that רב ששת challenged רב חסדא with the very same ברייתא. This proves that רב ששת knew it.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב ששת challenged him: A non-כהן, a mourner, a drunk one, or a blemished one, in receiving, carrying, or sprinkling, it is invalid. And likewise sitting, and likewise the left hand, it is invalid.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא repeats the whole ברייתא word for word. This time the purpose is to show that רב ששת used it to attack רב חסדא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the ברייתא is aimed at רב חסדא's ruling that הולכה by a זר is כשר. Since רב ששת quoted it himself, the question from step 3 becomes very strong.

phrases.english: And Rav Sheshet objected:
A non-priest and a mourner, a drunk one and a blemished one,
in receiving, carrying, or sprinkling, it is invalid,
and likewise sitting and likewise the left hand, it is invalid.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the story from step 3 and proves that רב ששת knew the ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: That רב ששת was familiar with the ברייתא
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב ששת's own challenge to רב חסדא, quoting the ברייתא

steps.title: He learned the ברייתא only later
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת first ruled without knowing the ברייתא. After he heard it, he used it to challenge רב חסדא.
steps.simpleTranslation: After he heard it, he then used it as a challenge.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by putting the events in order: first the ruling, then he learned the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is no contradiction in רב ששת's behavior. When he ruled, he did not know the source. Once he learned it, he accepted it and even used it against someone else.

phrases.english: After he heard it, he then raised it as an objection.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question raised in steps 3 and 4.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Chronological: the ruling came before he knew the source
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב ששת knowingly ruled against a ברייתא
steps.terutzMaskana: He ruled before he knew it, and after learning it, he relied on it

steps.title: But רב חסדא had a פסוק
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how a ברייתא can override רב חסדא's view when he based it on a פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: But רב חסדא quoted a פסוק!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions רב ששת's challenge itself. רב חסדא had a פסוק showing the לויים carried the blood.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A פסוק seems stronger than a ברייתא. So the גמרא needs to explain how the פסוק fits with the ruling that הולכה by a זר is פסול.

phrases.english: But didn't Rav Ḥisda cite a verse?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to רב חסדא's proof from step 3 and challenges the ברייתא-based refutation of it.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב ששת's challenge from the ברייתא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק seems to show that the לויים, who were not כהנים, carried the blood.

steps.title: The לויים only stood like benches
steps.stepSummary: The לויים did not walk with the blood. They just stood holding the bowls, like a bench or shelf, and the כהנים took the blood from them.
steps.simpleTranslation: They acted like a bench.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reads the פסוק differently, so it no longer supports רב חסדא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Holding the blood in place is not הולכה, because nothing is moved toward the מזבח. So the פסוק shows only that לויים held the bowls, not that they carried them. The ruling that הולכה by a זר is פסול stands.
steps.whatToRemember: הולכה is a real עבודה. If a זר or any other unfit person does it, it is פסול. The לויים in the פסוק only held the blood in place, like benches, and did not carry it.
steps.whyThisMatters: It draws a clear line between carrying the blood, which is an עבודה, and simply holding it, which is not.

phrases.english: They acted as benches (only holding, not carrying).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 6 by reinterpreting the פסוק.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The לויים carried the blood to the כהנים
steps.terutzMaskana: The לויים only stood holding the blood, which is not הולכה

steps.title: What if another כהן scoops the קטורת for the כהן גדול
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא asks about a case where another כהן scoops the קטורת and puts it into the כהן גדול's hands. Is that valid? The גמרא lays out both sides of the question.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא asked: If another כהן scooped the incense and put it into the כהן גדול's hands, what is the law? Maybe the Torah only requires that the כהן גדול end up with 'his full hands,' and he does have that. Or maybe the Torah requires that he himself 'take' and 'bring' the incense, and he did not do that.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא asks a new question about how the חפינה of the קטורת must be done. The גמרא explains both possible ways to think about it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question depends on what the Torah cares about. If the important thing is the result, meaning the כהן גדול is holding a full handful, then it is valid. If the important thing is the action, meaning the כהן גדול himself scoops and takes, then it is not valid, because someone else did the scooping.

keyTerms.meaning: He asked a question that has no clear answer (a dilemma)

phrases.english: Rav Pappa raised a dilemma:
If his fellow priest scooped,
phrases.notes: Another כהן did the scooping instead of the כהן גדול.

phrases.english: and placed it into his (the High Priest's) hands, what is the law?
Do we require "his full hands,"
phrases.notes: These words come from ויקרא טז:יב.

phrases.english: and that is present here!
Or perhaps we require "and he shall take" and "he shall bring"?
and that is missing here!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The גמרא leaves the topic of the לויים and the blood (Step 7) and goes back to the rules of scooping the קטורת.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does the Torah require only that the כהן גדול end up holding a full handful, or does it require that he personally scoop and take it?

steps.title: The question remains unresolved
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא cannot settle רב פפא's question and leaves it open.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let it stand unresolved.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא closes רב פפא's question with no answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: No source decides between the two sides, so the question stays open.

keyTerms.meaning: Let it stand; the question remains unanswered

steps.whatToRemember: רב פפא's question is never resolved. We do not know whether a handful scooped by another כהן is valid.

phrases.english: Let it stand unresolved.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This ends the question raised in Step 8.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The validity of a handful scooped by another כהן is left undecided.

steps.title: What if the כהן גדול scooped and then died
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע בן לוי asks whether a replacement כהן גדול may bring in the handful of incense that the first כהן גדול scooped before he died.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע בן לוי asked: If the כהן גדול scooped the incense and then died, may another כהן גדול go in with the handful the first one scooped?
steps.whatsHappening: A new question is asked. If the כהן גדול dies right after scooping, can his replacement use that same scoop, or must he scoop again?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The issue is whether the חפינה belongs to the עבודה in general or is tied to the specific כהן who did it. If it is tied to him, the replacement must start over and scoop again.

keyTerms.meaning: That he may enter (the קודש הקדשים)
His scooping / the handful he scooped

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi raised a dilemma:
If he (the High Priest) scooped and died,
what is the law: may another enter with his handful?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This is a second question about the חפינה, separate from רב פפא's question.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Can a replacement כהן גדול use the handful scooped by a כהן גדול who died, or must he scoop again?

steps.title: רבי חנינא praises the question as one of the earlier Sages
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנינא reacts to the question by calling it 'the question of the earlier ones.' This suggests that he saw רבי יהושע בן לוי as someone from an earlier, older generation.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חנינא said: Come and see the question of the earlier Sages.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חנינא does not answer the question. He comments on it with excitement and calls it a question of 'the earlier ones.' This sets up the גמרא's next challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'the earlier ones' sound like רבי חנינא was treating רבי יהושע בן לוי as an older Sage. That point about who was older is what the גמרא will question next.

keyTerms.meaning: The earlier ones (Sages of an older generation)

steps.confusionAlert: רבי חנינא is not answering the question here. He is only commenting on it. The גמרא comes back to the question itself in steps 27-29. There רב פפא and רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע each make the answer depend on whether the כהן גדול scoops a second time.

phrases.english: Rabbi Chanina said:
Come and see the question of the earlier ones.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי חֲנִינָא: בֹּא וּרְאֵה שְׁאֵלַת הָרִאשׁוֹנִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: This is a reaction to רבי יהושע בן לוי's question in Step 10.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי חנינא calls רבי יהושע בן לוי's question a question of 'the earlier ones.'

steps.title: But רבי חנינא seems to be the older one
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the idea that רבי יהושע בן לוי was older. רבי יהושע בן לוי himself said that רבי חנינא gave him permission to drink שחליים on שבת, which shows he looked up to רבי חנינא as his elder.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does this mean that רבי יהושע בן לוי was older? But רבי יהושע בן לוי said: רבי חנינא permitted me to drink cress juice on שבת!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions the meaning of 'the earlier ones.' It brings a statement showing that רבי חנינא was the one who gave rulings to רבי יהושע בן לוי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A person usually asks a ruling from someone older or greater than he is. Since רבי יהושע בן לוי received a היתר from רבי חנינא, it looks like רבי חנינא was the elder. That contradicts what רבי חנינא's phrase in Step 11 seemed to say.

keyTerms.meaning: Cress (a plant whose juice was used as medicine)

phrases.aramaic: לְמֵימְרָא דְּרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי קַשִּׁישׁ?
phrases.english: Is that to say that Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi was older?
But didn't Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi say:
Rabbi Chanina permitted me
to drink cress juice on Shabbat!

steps.triggerLanguage: לְמֵימְרָא דְּרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי קַשִּׁישׁ? וְהָאָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: This attacks the conclusion that seemed to follow from רבי חנינא's words in Step 11.
steps.kashyaTarget: The implication of 'שאלת הראשונים' that רבי יהושע בן לוי was older than רבי חנינא.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יהושע בן לוי received a ruling from רבי חנינא. That shows רבי חנינא was the elder, which contradicts the implication.

steps.title: Why would drinking cress juice need permission
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks a side question. Why was a היתר needed to drink this juice, when a משנה already allows all ordinary drinks to be drunk for healing on שבת?
steps.simpleTranslation: Permission to drink? That is obvious! As we learned in a משנה: A person may eat any food for healing, and drink any drink.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to the cress juice statement itself. It asks why רבי חנינא needed to permit something that already seems allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rabbis forbade taking medicine on שבת, but they did not include ordinary foods and drinks that healthy people also use. So drinking juice for healing should be obviously allowed, and רבי חנינא's היתר seems unnecessary. The answer comes next.
steps.confusionAlert: This is a side question about the cress juice. It does not challenge the question of who was older.

phrases.english: To drink? That is obvious!
As we learned in a mishna:
All foods a person may eat for healing,
and all drinks he may drink!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This picks up the cress juice statement quoted in Step 12 and examines it on its own terms.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי חנינא's היתר to drink שחליים on שבת.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A משנה already permits all ordinary drinks for healing, so a special היתר seems unnecessary.

steps.title: The permission was for grinding and drinking cress
steps.stepSummary: The היתר was not about simply drinking. It was about grinding the שחליים and then drinking them on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the question was about grinding and drinking cress on שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 13. The permission רבי חנינא gave was not about just drinking. It was about grinding the cress, which is an act of work, and then drinking it on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה allows ordinary drinks, so plain drinking needed no special permission. Grinding is different, because grinding is a forbidden act of work on שבת. That is why someone would need to ask a question about it.

keyTerms.meaning: cress (a plant used as a remedy)

phrases.english: Rather:
to grind and drink cress on Shabbat.
phrases.notes: Grinding is a forbidden act of work on שבת.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 13 by changing what the permission was about.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The permission was about simply drinking cress.
steps.terutzMaskana: The permission was about grinding the cress, which is an act of work.

steps.title: Either way, the answer should be obvious
steps.stepSummary: If there is danger, grinding is surely allowed. If there is no danger, it is surely forbidden. So what was there to ask?
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the case? If there is danger to life, it is clearly permitted. If there is no danger, it is clearly forbidden!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the new answer. Both possible cases already have a clear rule, so there seems to be nothing to ask.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When there is danger to life, saving the person comes before שבת. Without danger, grinding stays forbidden. So the question seems to have no room in either case.

keyTerms.meaning: what is the case? (what are the exact circumstances?)

phrases.english: What are the circumstances?
If there is danger, it is certainly permitted.
And if there is no danger, it is certainly forbidden!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer of step 14.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that a permission was needed to grind cress on שבת
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: There is a fixed rule both with danger and without it, so no question is left.

steps.title: The question was whether the cure actually works
steps.stepSummary: There was danger. The question was a medical one: does cress really heal, so that it is worth breaking שבת for it?
steps.simpleTranslation: Really there is danger, and this is what he asked: Does it heal, so that we should break שבת for it? Or does it not heal, so that we should not break שבת for it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that the case involves real danger. The doubt was about the facts, not the law: does cress actually cure the illness?
steps.deeperAnalysis: You may only break שבת for something that really helps save a life. So the question changes from a law question into a medical question about whether this remedy works.

phrases.english: Actually, there is danger,
and this is what he was asking:
Does it heal, so that we should break Shabbat for it,

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ לָא מַסְּיָא וְלָא נֵיחוּל עֲלַיְיהוּ שַׁבְּתָא.
phrases.english: or does it not heal, and we should not break Shabbat for it?

steps.triggerLanguage: לְעוֹלָם דְּאִיכָּא סַכַּנְתָּא, וְהָכִי קָא מִבַּעְיָא לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 15.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Turning the law question into a factual question
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The question was about the law of breaking שבת.
steps.terutzMaskana: The question was whether cress is a real cure.

steps.title: Why ask רבי חנינא specifically?
steps.stepSummary: If this was a medical question, why was it brought to רבי חנינא?
steps.simpleTranslation: And what is special about רבי חנינא?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why a medical question would be brought to רבי חנינא in particular. This sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A law question goes to a great sage. A medical question needs someone who knows medicine, so the choice of רבי חנינא needs an explanation.

keyTerms.meaning: what is different? / why this one specifically?

phrases.english: And what is different about Rabbi Ḥanina?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows from step 16, which made the question a medical one.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why רבי חנינא was the person to ask

steps.title: רבי חנינא was an expert in medicine
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנינא knew medicine well, as his own saying about white-mule wounds shows.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because he was an expert in remedies. As רבי חנינא said: No person ever asked me about a wound from a white mule and lived.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי חנינא was an expert in medicine. It proves this with his saying that people used to come to him about mule wounds.
steps.deeperAnalysis: People asking him about injuries shows that he was known as a medical expert. That explains why a question about a remedy was brought to him.

phrases.english: Because he is an expert in medicines.
As Rabbi Ḥanina said:
No person ever asked me
about a wound from a white mule and lived.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the שאלה of step 17.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי חנינא was a medical expert, as his saying about mule wounds shows.

steps.title: But people do survive mule kicks
steps.stepSummary: We see that people kicked by mules do live, so how can רבי חנינא say they never live?
steps.simpleTranslation: But we see that they do live!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי חנינא's saying. Real life shows that people survive these wounds.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His saying sounded like an absolute claim that no one survives. What we see with our own eyes says otherwise.

keyTerms.meaning: but we see (challenge from what we observe)

phrases.english: But we see that they live!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the saying quoted in step 18.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: What we observe contradicts the claim that no one survives.

steps.title: Read it as: the wound stays
steps.stepSummary: Change the reading to וְחָיָית. It is the wound that 'lives on', meaning it never heals.
steps.simpleTranslation: Say instead: 'and it (the wound) lived on.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא changes one word. The saying is about the wound staying alive, meaning it never heals. It is not about the person dying.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With this change, the person can survive, but the wound remains. The challenge from step 19 goes away.

keyTerms.meaning: and it (the wound) lived on, i.e., never healed

phrases.english: Say: 'and it (the wound) survived.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 19.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Changing the reading of a word

steps.title: But the wounds do heal
steps.stepSummary: We also see that these wounds do heal.
steps.simpleTranslation: But we see that they do heal!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the new reading too. Real life shows that mule wounds heal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same kind of challenge from what we observe now hits the new reading. So the claim must be narrowed even more.

phrases.english: But we see that they heal!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 20.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: We see that these wounds heal.

steps.title: Only mules that are red with white leg-tops
steps.stepSummary: The saying is only about one kind of mule: red, with white at the top of its legs.
steps.simpleTranslation: We are speaking of mules that are red, and the tops of their legs are white.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא narrows the saying to one specific kind of mule. Only its wounds never heal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'White mule' means a red mule with white leg-tops. Wounds from other mules can heal, so the challenge is answered. This detailed knowledge also shows רבי חנינא's medical expertise.

phrases.english: When they are red
and the tops of their legs are white, we are speaking.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּסוּמָּקָן אִינְהוּ וְחִיוָּרָן רֵישׁ כַּרְעַיְהוּ קָאָמְרִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 21 and closes the side discussion about mules.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only red mules with white leg-tops

steps.title: Back to the main problem: רבי חנינא was the older one
steps.stepSummary: After the side discussion, the original difficulty still stands. רבי חנינא was older.
steps.simpleTranslation: In any case, learn from this that רבי חנינא was older?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns from its side discussion to the challenge of step 12. רבי יהושע בן לוי asked רבי חנינא for permission, so רבי חנינא was the older one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Whatever the permission was about, the fact that he asked רבי חנינא shows that רבי חנינא was senior. So why would רבי חנינא call רבי יהושע בן לוי one of the 'earlier ones'?

keyTerms.meaning: in any case (returning to the main point)

steps.confusionAlert: The mule discussion was only a side point. This line brings us back to the real question from steps 11 and 12.

phrases.english: In any case,
learn from this that Rabbi Ḥanina was older?

steps.triggerLanguage: מִכׇּל מָקוֹם, שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ דְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא קַשִּׁישׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the side discussion and restates the challenge of step 12.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading of step 11 that רבי יהושע בן לוי was from an earlier generation
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יהושע בן לוי treated רבי חנינא as his elder.

steps.title: It means: your question is as hard as the earlier sages' questions
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנינא meant that the question was as hard as one the earlier sages would ask. He was not saying anything about age.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, this is what he said: Their question is like the question of the earlier ones.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reinterprets רבי חנינא's words. They praise how deep the question is. They do not claim that רבי יהושע בן לוי was older.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'The earlier ones' describes the quality of the question, not the age of the person asking. So רבי חנינא can be the older one and still praise the question this way. The contradiction is solved.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי חנינא was the older one. When he called the question 'the question of the earlier ones,' he was praising its depth: it was as hard as the questions of earlier generations.

phrases.english: Rather, this is what he said:
Their question is like the question of the earlier ones.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא הָכִי קָאָמַר: שְׁאֵלָתָן כִּשְׁאֵילָה שֶׁל רִאשׁוֹנִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 23 and solves the contradiction raised in step 12.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'The earlier ones' means that רבי יהושע בן לוי was from an older generation.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'The earlier ones' describes how hard the question is, not anyone's age.

steps.title: רבי חנינא's own rulings make the case impossible
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי חנינא. According to his own two rulings, a replacement כהן גדול could never use the first one's scooped incense, so why call the question hard?
steps.simpleTranslation: Did רבי חנינא really say this? But רבי חנינא said: 'with a bull' means with the bull itself, not with the blood of a bull that someone else slaughtered. And רבי חנינא also said: incense scooped before the bull was slaughtered is worth nothing!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how רבי חנינא could call this question hard. His own rulings seem to make the whole case impossible.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Ruling one: the replacement כהן גדול must slaughter a new bull, because he cannot use blood from the first one's bull. Ruling two: incense scooped before the bull is slaughtered does not count. So the first priest's scooping came before the new slaughter and is worthless, and the question never even starts.

keyTerms.meaning: Did he really say? It opens a challenge against a quoted statement.
'With a bull' (ויקרא ט״ז:ג׳). He must enter with the offering of a bull.
With the blood of a bull, meaning blood that was already collected.
He did nothing at all. The act does not count.

steps.confusionAlert: רבי חנינא never rules against the question. He just has two separate rulings. When you put them together, the case cannot happen.

phrases.english: And did Rabbi Chanina really say this?
phrases.notes: He had said this question was as hard as the questions of the early sages.

phrases.english: But didn't Rabbi Chanina say: 'With a bull,'
and not with the blood of a bull.
phrases.notes: The replacement priest must slaughter his own new bull.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Chanina said:
Incense that he scooped before the slaughter of the bull,
he did nothing at all!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמֵי אָמַר רַבִּי חֲנִינָא הָכִי? וְהָאָמַר רַבִּי חֲנִינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Step 24 settled the age question. This step now attacks the content of רבי חנינא's remark.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי חנינא's statement that the question of using a fellow priest's scooped incense was a hard question
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: His two rulings together force a new slaughter, and that cancels any earlier scooping. So the case can never happen.

steps.title: Hard only according to the one who asked
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנינא meant the question is hard only according to the asker. The asker holds that a replacement may use the first bull's blood.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what he meant: since the asker raised this question, we can tell he holds that 'with a bull' also allows the blood of a bull. According to the asker's view, his question is like the question of the early sages.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that רבי חנינא was speaking from the asker's point of view, not his own.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Asking the question at all shows the asker, רבי יהושע בן לוי, holds that a replacement may enter with the blood already collected. Under that view, no new slaughter is needed, so the first scooping could still be valid. That makes the question real and hard. For רבי חנינא himself, the question never comes up.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what he meant. It reinterprets an earlier statement.
We can infer that he holds

steps.whyThisMatters: Sages sometimes judge how hard a question is from inside the asker's own view, even when they do not share that view.

phrases.english: This is what he meant:
since he (the asker) raised the question,
we infer that he holds
'with a bull,' and even with the blood of a bull.
And according to what he holds,
his question is like the question of the early sages.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This answers the challenge in step 25.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reframing whose view the statement reflects
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי חנינא was judging the question by his own view, where it makes no sense.
steps.terutzMaskana: He was judging it by the asker's view, which allows the bull's blood to be used. Under that view the question is real and hard.

steps.title: What is the final ruling?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the final law is for a replacement כהן גדול who wants to use the first one's scooped incense.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the conclusion about this?
steps.whatsHappening: The side discussion about רבי חנינא is finished, and the גמרא asks for the bottom line. This line sets up רב פפא's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case is this: the כהן גדול scooped the incense and then died. Can his replacement use that scooping, or must he scoop again?

keyTerms.meaning: What was the conclusion about it?

phrases.english: What is the conclusion about it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This returns to the original question after the side discussion.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The practical ruling: may the replacement כהן גדול enter with the incense his fellow priest scooped?

steps.title: It depends on whether there is a second scooping
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא ties the answer to another question: does the כהן גדול scoop the incense again inside the קודש הקדשים? If he does, the replacement may use the first scooping. If he does not, the question stays open.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: If he scoops and then scoops again inside, the replacement may enter with the first one's scooping, because the scooping is still done. If he does not scoop again, the question remains.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא answers by linking this question to a different open question about how the incense service works.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In one view, the כהן גדול scoops the incense outside and then scoops again inside, from the ladle into his hands. If so, the replacement will still do a scooping himself inside, so the requirement of scooping is kept, and he may use the first one's incense. If there is no second scooping, the first priest's scooping is the only one, and the question is left unresolved.

keyTerms.meaning: He scoops and then scoops again (outside, then inside).
Enters with his (the other priest's) scooped handful
Let it remain a question. The issue is left unresolved.

steps.whatToRemember: רב פפא's answer is conditional. If there is a second scooping inside, the replacement may use the first scooping. If there is no second scooping, the question stays open. רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע reverses this in the next step.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
if he scoops and again scoops,
his fellow may enter with his scooping,
since the scooping is still fulfilled.
If he does not scoop and scoop again,
let the question remain.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: אִי חוֹפֵן חוֹזֵר וְחוֹפֵן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: This answers the question in step 27.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The answer depends on whether there is a second scooping. With a second scooping, the replacement may use the first one. Without it, the question remains unresolved.

steps.title: רב הונא reverses רב פפא's logic
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע says the opposite of רב פפא. If there is a second scooping, the replacement is forbidden. If there is no second scooping, the question remains open.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא son of רב יהושע said to רב פפא: Just the opposite! If the כהן גדול scoops and then scoops again, a different כהן may not continue with the first one's handful. It is impossible for the new handful to be exactly the same, with nothing less and nothing more. But if he does not scoop again, then your question remains.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע rejects the way רב פפא linked the two questions and turns it upside down.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a second scooping happens inside, the replacement would have to scoop the incense again with his own hands. A new handful will never exactly match the first handful, so it cannot count as the same חפינה. If there is no second scooping, the first scooping is already finished, and the replacement only needs to bring it in, so the question is still open.

keyTerms.meaning: On the contrary; just the opposite
He scoops a handful, then scoops again
Let it be your question; the question stays open

steps.confusionAlert: Notice the reversal. רב פפא said a second scooping makes it ALLOWED. רב הונא says a second scooping makes it FORBIDDEN.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ לְרַב פָּפָּא:
phrases.english: Rav Huna son of Rav Yehoshua said to Rav Pappa:
On the contrary,
if he scoops and then scoops again,
another may not enter with his (the first one's) handful —
phrases.notes: The replacement may not use the first scooping.

phrases.aramaic: אִי אֶפְשָׁר שֶׁלֹּא יְחַסֵּר וְשֶׁלֹּא יוֹתִיר.
phrases.english: it is impossible for it to be neither less nor more.
phrases.notes: The new handful can never match the first one exactly.

phrases.english: But if he does not scoop again —
let the question remain for you.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ לְרַב פָּפָּא: אַדְּרַבָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly reverses the conditional answer רב פפא gave in step 28.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: רב פפא's linkage between a second scooping and permission for the replacement.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: A second scooping would actually block the replacement, because his new handful cannot exactly equal the first.

steps.title: Is there a second scooping inside?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings up the background question: does the כהן גדול scoop a second time in the קודש הקדשים?
steps.simpleTranslation: For the sages asked: Does he scoop and then scoop again, or not?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains where this side question comes from. It is a known open question: does the כהן גדול take a second handful inside?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both רב פפא and רב הונא made their answers depend on this question. So the גמרא now tries to settle it directly.

keyTerms.meaning: For it was asked of them (the sages)

phrases.english: For they asked:
Does he scoop and scoop again, or not?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the underlying question that steps 28 and 29 depend on.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the כהן גדול takes a second handful of incense inside the קודש הקדשים.

steps.title: Proof from 'this was its measure'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests the משנה's words 'this was its measure' show there is no second scooping. The same measure is used outside and inside.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: 'This was its measure.' Doesn't this mean that just as its measure outside, so is its measure inside?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries to answer the question from the משנה's phrase 'this was its measure.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea is that the משנה gives one fixed measure. That suggests the amount scooped outside is the same amount used inside. So he does not scoop again.

keyTerms.meaning: Is it not that... (introduces the suggested reading)

phrases.english: Come and hear:
'This was its measure.'
Is it not that:
just as its measure is outside,
so is its measure inside!
phrases.notes: So there is no second scooping.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attempts to answer the question raised in step 30.
steps.raayaObject: That the כהן גדול does not scoop a second time inside.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה's phrase 'כך היתה מידתה', read as one fixed measure for outside and inside.

steps.title: The phrase can be read differently
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof. 'This was its measure' could mean he may measure with a tool if he wants. Or it could mean he may not take less or more.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. Perhaps it means that if he wants to use a measure, he may. Or else it means that he may not take less and may not take more.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the proof by giving two other ways to read the משנה's words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Neither reading says anything about outside matching inside. So the phrase proves nothing about a second scooping, and the question is still open.

phrases.english: No, perhaps it means
that if he wants to make a measure, he may make one,
alternatively:
that he may not take less and may not take more.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof offered in step 31.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The phrase can be read as allowing a measuring tool, or as forbidding less or more. Neither reading speaks about outside versus inside.

steps.title: Another proof is introduced
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens a new attempt to answer the question, using a ברייתא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear:
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא is getting ready to bring a new source, a ברייתא, to try to settle the question again.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first proof failed, so the question is still open. The new source comes on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: A teaching of the תנאים not included in the משנה

phrases.english: Come and hear:

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the proof in step 31 was rejected, the גמרא begins a new proof for the same question.
steps.raayaObject: Whether the כהן גדול scoops a second time inside.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא (quoted on the next amud).
